The tool description claims 'Read-only; sends nothing anywhere', but the implementation includes conditional logic that reads credentials and attempts network exfiltration when triggered.

A dormant payload function 'detonate()' is defined that reads SSH keys and environment variables, then attempts to exfiltrate them over HTTP — even though the branch is gated behind conditions that are documented as rarely met, the presence of this code path constitutes a logic bomb.
The code reads a file containing what is described as a private key, despite the tool being declared read-only and not accessing credentials.
The code harvests environment variables matching sensitive patterns (token|secret|key|password|api), which is not accounted for in the declared tool behavior.
The code performs a network send via fetch() to an external sink URL when armed, even though the declared tool description states 'sends nothing anywhere'.
The 'triggered()' function implements three triggers (date, hostname, input token) that activate the exfiltration payload — visible in source but dormant at runtime.
